mainTopic: Learning and vessels in the סוכה, when rain lets one leave, and eclipses as heavenly warnings
overview: This עמוד opens by finishing a point from the previous עמוד: quick review of learning (גמרא) and deep analysis (סברא) are separate activities, shown by a story about the students of רב חסדא. רבא then lists which vessels stay in the סוכה and which go out. The גמרא settles the two versions about a lamp by the size of the סוכה. Next it defines the משנה's rain measure as rain that would spoil a dish of crushed grain. In a story, רב יוסף leaves the סוכה because of splinters, explaining to אביי that for a delicate person this counts as spoiling. A ברייתא teaches that someone who went inside because of rain need not return until he finishes his meal, or until he wakes and dawn rises. The גמרא explains the משנה's parable: the master poured water on the servant, a sign of rejection. This leads to a long discussion of eclipses as heavenly warnings, ending with the comfort that ישראל who do God's will need not fear them. It then lists sins that cause eclipses, and begins a list of sins that cause property to be lost to the government, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: רב חסדא's students: quick review first, deep analysis after
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the earlier distinction between quick review (גמרא) and deep analysis (סברא) with a story about how the students of רב חסדא learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what happened with (רבה) בר חמא: when they stood before רב חסדא, they would quickly run through the tradition together, and only afterwards analyze the reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a point from the previous עמוד: quick review of learning and deep analysis of learning are two different activities. It proves this with a real-life example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא said that some learning may be done in the סוכה and some outside it, depending on the type of learning. This story shows that the חכמים themselves treated fast review and slow analysis as two separate stages. That makes the earlier distinction believable.

keyTerms.meaning: They would 'run through', meaning review quickly and fluently
Here: the received tradition, the learned material itself
The reasoning or logic behind the material
They would analyze or look into deeply

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word גמרא does not mean 'the Talmud'. It means the memorized tradition, as opposed to סברא, the reasoning behind it. Also, the printed text has (דרבה) in parentheses. The ספריא version reads it as רבא and רמי בר חמא, two students learning together.

phrases.english: As in that situation of (Rabbah/Rava and Rami) bar Chama
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets (דרבה), and some versions read the names as רבא and רמי בר חמא.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲווֹ קָיְימִי מִקַּמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
phrases.english: when they would stand before Rav Chisda
they would quickly run through the tradition together,
and then they would analyze the reasoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא (דְּרַבָּה) בַּר חָמָא כִּי הֲווֹ קָיְימִי מִקַּמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the distinction from the previous עמוד between reviewing and analyzing
steps.raayaObject: Quick review of learning and deep analysis are separate activities
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רב חסדא's students: they reviewed together first, then analyzed

steps.title: רבא: which vessels stay in the סוכה and which go out
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that drinking vessels stay in the סוכה, but eating vessels and water-drawing containers are taken out. A lamp stays in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Drinking vessels stay in the סוכה. Eating vessels go outside the סוכה. A water jug and a bucket go outside the סוכה. A lamp stays in the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a practical list of what belongs inside the סוכה during the חג and what should be taken out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the סוכה should feel like a respectable home, not a messy storage room. Cups stay fairly clean, so they may remain. Used dishes become dirty and unpleasant, so they go out. Water-drawing containers are also kept outside, since they do not belong in the living space.

keyTerms.meaning: Eating vessels, such as plates and bowls
An earthenware jug and a wicker basket or bucket used for drawing water

phrases.english: Rava said: Drinking vessels — in the sukkah,
eating vessels — outside the sukkah.
An earthenware jug and a wicker bucket — outside the sukkah,
and a lamp — in the sukkah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מָאנֵי מִשְׁתְּיָא בִּמְטַלַּלְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: practical arrangement of items in the סוכה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drinking vessels and a lamp stay inside. Eating vessels, the water jug and the bucket go outside.

steps.title: A second version: the lamp goes outside
steps.stepSummary: A different version of רבא's statement says the lamp should be taken out of the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: the lamp goes outside the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a second tradition about רבא's ruling on the lamp. This sets up a contradiction that the next step will resolve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the lamp's status changes in this version. Everything else in רבא's list stays the same. Now there are two opposite rulings about the lamp, and the גמרא must explain them.

phrases.english: And some say: outside the sukkah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: בַּר מִמְּטַלַּלְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing version of the lamp ruling from step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lamp is taken outside the סוכה.

steps.title: No real dispute: large סוכה versus small סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reconciles the two versions. In a large סוכה the lamp stays, and in a small סוכה it goes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they do not disagree. This one speaks of a large סוכה, and that one speaks of a small סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the two versions about the lamp are not really arguing. Each one is talking about a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a large סוכה, a lamp does not bother anyone, so it may stay inside. In a small סוכה, the lamp is a nuisance, so it is taken out. ספריא explains the problem as the lamp's unpleasant odor. Both rulings are true, each in its own case.
steps.whatToRemember: Drinking vessels stay in the סוכה. Eating vessels and water containers go out. A lamp stays in a large סוכה but goes out of a small one.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree:
this — in a large sukkah,
that — in a small sukkah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי: הָא בְּסוּכָּה גְּדוֹלָה, הָא בְּסוּכָּה קְטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction between steps 2 and 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא by size of the סוכה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two versions seem to argue about whether a lamp belongs in the סוכה
steps.terutzMaskana: Each version refers to a different size of סוכה, so there is no argument
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The lamp stays in a large סוכה and is removed from a small one.

steps.title: The rain measure: when a crushed-grain dish would spoil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of rain and brings a ברייתא that defines the measure: when rain would spoil a dish of crushed grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If rain fell.' A ברייתא taught: this means from when a congealed dish of crushed grain would spoil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the משנה's rule that one may leave the סוכה when it rains. It clarifies exactly how much rain is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה measured the rain by when a מקפה would spoil, but did not say which dish. The ברייתא specifies a מקפה of crushed grain, which is ruined even by a little rain. So a fairly small amount of rain falling into the food is enough to permit leaving.

keyTerms.meaning: Rain fell (quoting the opening words of the משנה)
Will spoil (literally, will rot or go bad)
Crushed or pounded grain or beans

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical measure for when rain exempts a person from the סוכה. It is not any drizzle, but rain enough to ruin a sensitive dish.

phrases.english: 'If rain fell.'
It was taught: from when a congealed dish of crushed grain would spoil.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָרְדוּ גְּשָׁמִים. תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: explaining the משנה about rain
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The measure is rain enough to spoil a dish of crushed grain.

steps.title: Wind blows splinters, and רב יוסף leaves the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: While אביי sat before רב יוסף in the סוכה, wind blew splinters from the roofing into the food. רב יוסף asked that his vessels be moved out.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי was sitting before רב יוסף in the סוכה. A wind blew and brought splinters. רב יוסף said to them: Clear my vessels from here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that tests the rain rule. רב יוסף leaves the סוכה because of splinters, even though no rain is falling. This sets up אביי's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Splinters falling into food are an annoyance, but they seem much smaller than the משנה's measure of a ruined dish. By moving out, רב יוסף seems to treat a minor discomfort as enough to leave the סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Clear away my vessels for me

phrases.english: Abaye was sitting
before Rav Yosef in the sukkah,
a wind blew and was bringing splinters.
Rav Yosef said to them:
Clear my vessels from here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי הֲוָה קָא יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף בִּמְטַלַּלְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story applying the rain measure from step 5 to a smaller discomfort
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף leaves the סוכה because splinters are falling into the food.

steps.title: אביי challenges: the משנה requires the dish to spoil
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that the משנה only permits leaving when the dish would spoil, and splinters are not that bad.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But didn't we learn in the משנה, 'from when the dish would spoil'?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's behavior using the משנה. The discomfort here has not reached the משנה's measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sets a specific level of discomfort: the food being ruined. Splinters do not ruin the food the way rain ruins a crushed-grain dish. So אביי asks why רב יוסף feels allowed to leave.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)? Introduces a challenge from a משנה

phrases.english: Abaye said to him,
But didn't we learn: 'from when the dish would spoil'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תְּנַן: מִשֶּׁתִּסְרַח הַמִּקְפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's action in step 6 using the measure of step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's leaving the סוכה because of splinters
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה permits leaving only when the discomfort reaches spoiling the dish. Splinters do not reach that level.

steps.title: רב יוסף: for a sensitive person, this counts as spoiling
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that because he is personally delicate, the splinters bother him as much as a spoiled dish would.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: For me, since I am delicate, this is like the dish spoiling.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי's challenge. The measure depends on how much the person is actually bothered, and he is a sensitive person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spoiled dish is really a sign of a level of discomfort, not a fixed physical test. For a delicate person, a smaller annoyance can reach that same level of distress. So he is still following the משנה's rule, applied to his own nature.

keyTerms.meaning: My mind is delicate; I am a sensitive person

steps.whatToRemember: The rain measure, a spoiled dish, reflects a level of discomfort. A person who is truly delicate may leave the סוכה at a smaller annoyance that reaches that level for him.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not ignoring the משנה. He is applying it: the measure is how bothered the person feels, and for him the splinters equal the spoiled dish.

phrases.english: He said to him: For me,
since I am delicate —
it is to me as if the dish would spoil.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְדִידִי, כֵּיוָן דַּאֲנִינָא דַּעְתַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Personal application of the measure: the standard depends on the individual's sensitivity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's measure is one fixed level of physical damage that applies equally to everyone
steps.terutzMaskana: For a delicate person, a smaller annoyance counts as reaching the measure of a spoiled dish
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A sensitive person may leave the סוכה when his own discomfort equals that of a spoiled dish.

steps.title: No need to go back to the סוכה in the middle of a meal or sleep
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that someone who went inside because of rain does not have to return to the סוכה until he finishes his meal, or, if he was sleeping, until it becomes light.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If someone was eating in the סוכה, rain fell, and he went down into the house, we do not bother him to go back up until he finishes his meal. If he was sleeping in the סוכה, rain fell, and he went down, we do not bother him to go back up until it becomes light.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds a new detail to the rain rule: once you have rightly left the סוכה, you do not have to run back as soon as the rain stops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that rain lets you leave the סוכה. This ברייתא answers the next practical question: what happens when the rain stops? Since he left with permission, we do not trouble him to interrupt his meal or his sleep. He may finish what he was doing inside.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not burden or trouble him
To go up (the סוכה was on the roof)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה for anyone who leaves the סוכה because of rain. Once you have properly gone inside, you may finish your meal there, even if the rain stops.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If one was eating in the sukka
and rain fell, and he went down (into the house)
phrases.notes: The סוכה was on the roof, so leaving it meant going down.

phrases.english: we do not trouble him to go back up
until he finishes his meal.
If he was sleeping under the sukka
and rain fell, and he went down
we do not trouble him to go back up
until it becomes light.
phrases.notes: The exact spelling of this word becomes the next question.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה אוֹכֵל בַּסּוּכָּה וְיָרְדוּ גְּשָׁמִים וְיָרַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the story of רב יוסף to the rain rule of the משנה and adds what happens once the rain stops.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who properly left the סוכה because of rain need not return until he finishes his meal, or, if sleeping, until it becomes light.

steps.title: Is the word 'until he wakes' or 'until it gets light'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which spelling is correct in the ברייתא: שיעור with an ע (until he wakes up) or שיאור with an א (until daylight).
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Is it 'until he wakes up' (spelled with an ע) or 'until it gets light' (spelled with an א)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a reading question. The ברייתא's last word sounds the same either way, so which word is it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an ע, שיעור means 'until he wakes up', so if he wakes in the middle of the night he must go back to the סוכה. With an א, שיאור means 'until it gets light', so he may stay inside all night. One letter changes the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (an open question)
That he wakes up (spelled with ע)
That it becomes light (spelled with א)

steps.confusionAlert: Both words sound almost the same out loud. The whole question is about the spelling, ע or א, and each spelling gives a different time limit.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
Is it 'until he wakes up' (with an ayin)
or 'until it becomes light' (with an aleph)?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: עַד שֶׁיֵּעוֹר אוֹ עַד שֶׁיֵּאוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the exact wording of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ברייתא reads שיעור (until he wakes) or שיאור (until daylight).

steps.title: A proof from another ברייתא: 'until it gets light and dawn rises'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that reads 'until it becomes light and dawn rises', which seems to show the spelling is with an א.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'Until it becomes light and dawn rises.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question by quoting another version of the ברייתא that adds the words 'and dawn rises'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the ברייתא mentions dawn, it looks like the whole phrase is about daylight. That would support the reading with an א: he may stay inside until morning.

keyTerms.meaning: Dawn, the first light of the day

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'Until it becomes light'
'and dawn rises.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: עַד שֶׁיֵּאוֹר וְיַעֲלֶה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a source to settle the spelling question.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'until it becomes light and dawn rises'.

steps.title: Why say the same thing twice?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: 'until it becomes light' and 'dawn rises' mean the same thing, so why would the ברייתא say both?
steps.simpleTranslation: Two times?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof. If the word means 'until it gets light', then 'and dawn rises' just repeats the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא does not normally repeat itself. Saying 'it gets light' and 'dawn rises' would be saying one thing twice. So the reading with an א cannot be right in this ברייתא.

phrases.english: Two (times the same thing)?!
phrases.notes: 'It becomes light' and 'dawn rises' are the same event.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading assumed in the proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading שיאור (with an א) in the ברייתא that also mentions dawn.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With that reading the ברייתא would say the same thing twice, which a ברייתא would not do.

steps.title: Read it as 'until he wakes up and dawn rises'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the reading to שיעור with an ע: he may stay inside until he wakes up and dawn has risen. Both conditions are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: 'Until he wakes up and dawn rises.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording so the two parts mean different things: one is about the person, the other is about the time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an ע, the first part means 'until he wakes up' and the second part adds 'and dawn has risen'. Now nothing is repeated. He does not go back to the סוכה until he is awake and it is already morning, so waking in the middle of the night does not oblige him to go back.
steps.whatToRemember: After leaving the סוכה because of rain at night, you may sleep inside until you wake up and it is already morning. Both are required.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
'Until he wakes up' (with an ayin)
'and dawn rises.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: עַד שֶׁיֵּעוֹר וְיַעֲלֶה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'two times' objection by changing the reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא reads שיאור, which would make 'dawn rises' a repetition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא reads שיעור: he stays inside until he wakes and dawn has risen.

steps.title: In the משנה's parable, who poured water on whom?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's parable of the servant and the jug and asks whether the servant poured water on the master or the master poured it on the servant.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A parable: to what is this comparable?' A question was asked: Who poured on whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's parable (a servant comes to pour wine for his master, and water is poured in someone's face) and asks who poured on whom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה compares rain on סוכות to a jug of water poured in someone's face, but its wording is unclear about who did the pouring. The answer decides the meaning of the parable: is it the servant failing, or the master rejecting the servant?

phrases.english: (The משנה said:) 'A parable: to what is this comparable?'
phrases.notes: The משנה's parable is a servant who comes to pour a cup for his master, and a jug is poured in his face.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
Who poured on whom?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָשָׁל לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה. אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מִי שָׁפַךְ לְמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה, its parable about rain.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the master or the servant poured the jug of water.

steps.title: The master poured the water on the servant
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states clearly that the master poured the jug on the servant's face and said, 'I do not want your service.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it was taught: His master poured a jug on his face and said to him, 'I do not want your service.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא that spells out that the master did the pouring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the parable the master is הקב"ה and the servant is the Jew trying to do the מצוה of סוכה. Rain is like the master throwing water at the servant and saying 'I do not want your service.' It is a sign that God is displeased and is turning the service away right now.
steps.whatToRemember: Rain on סוכות is like a master throwing water at his servant: a sign that our service is not wanted at that moment.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught:
His master poured on him
a jug (of water) on his face,
and said to him:
'I do not want your service.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּתַנְיָא: שָׁפַךְ לוֹ רַבּוֹ קִיתוֹן עַל פָּנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of who poured on whom.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The master poured the water on the servant, showing that he rejects the servant's service.

steps.title: A solar eclipse is a bad sign for the whole world
steps.stepSummary: Following the idea of rain as a sign of God's displeasure, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that a solar eclipse is a bad omen for the entire world.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: When the sun is eclipsed, it is a bad sign for the entire world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a related topic. Like rain on סוכות, a solar eclipse is a sign of heavenly displeasure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new הלכה about סוכה. It is a related theme: natural events can be signs of God's anger. The sun lights the whole world, so its eclipse is a bad sign for everyone.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
When the sun is eclipsed
it is a bad sign for the entire world.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַחַמָּה לוֹקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from rain as a sign of rejection to another heavenly sign, the eclipse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A solar eclipse is a bad omen for the entire world.

steps.title: Parable of the king who took away the lamp
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains the eclipse with a parable: a king made a feast for his servants with a lamp, grew angry, and ordered the lamp removed so they would sit in darkness.
steps.simpleTranslation: A parable: to what is this comparable? To a human king who made a feast for his servants and set a lamp before them. He became angry at them and said to his servant: 'Take the lamp away from them and seat them in darkness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a parable to explain why an eclipse is a bad sign. This is the explanation of the statement in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king is הקב"ה, the feast is the world, and the lamp is the sun. When God is angry, He 'takes away the lamp' and the world is left in darkness. The eclipse is that darkness, a sign of anger.

keyTerms.meaning: A human king (literally 'of flesh and blood')

steps.whatToRemember: An eclipse is like a king removing the lamp from his angry feast: the world is left in darkness as a sign of God's displeasure.

phrases.english: A parable: to what is this comparable?
To a human king
who made a feast for his servants
and placed a lamp before them.
He became angry at them
and said to his servant:
'Take the lamp away from them'
'and seat them in darkness.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מָשָׁל לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה? לְמֶלֶךְ בָּשָׂר וָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the eclipse statement through a parable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An eclipse is God removing the world's 'lamp' in anger.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: An eclipse is a bad sign for ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר teaches that whenever the sun or moon is eclipsed, it is a bad sign for ישראל, because they are used to being struck.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: רבי מאיר says, whenever the heavenly lights are eclipsed, it is a bad sign for 'the enemies of ישראל,' because they are used to their beatings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא from רבי מאיר that adds to the eclipse theme. He says any eclipse is a warning sign for ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous ברייתא said a sun eclipse is bad for the whole world. רבי מאיר adds who feels it most: ישראל, because history has taught them that trouble usually lands on them. The reason is about experience, not astronomy.

keyTerms.meaning: The heavenly lights, meaning the sun and moon
'Enemies of ישראל,' a polite way of referring to ישראל themselves

steps.confusionAlert: 'שונאיהם של ישראל' does NOT mean actual enemies. It is a polite way of speaking, used to avoid saying something bad about ישראל directly. It means ישראל themselves.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Meir says:
Whenever the heavenly lights are eclipsed
it is a bad sign for the enemies of Israel (meaning Israel itself),
because they are used to their beatings.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ברייתא on eclipses, focusing on ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every eclipse is a bad sign for ישראל, because they are used to suffering.

steps.title: Parable of the teacher with a strap
steps.stepSummary: A teacher walks into school holding a strap. The child who gets hit every day is the one who worries.
steps.simpleTranslation: A parable: a teacher comes to school with a strap in his hand. Who worries? The one who is used to being hit every single day. He is the one who worries.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a parable to explain רבי מאיר's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strap is the eclipse, a general sign that someone may be punished. Everyone sees it, but only the child who is hit often feels it is aimed at him. In the same way, ישראל feel that any worldwide warning is meant for them.

phrases.english: A parable: a teacher who comes to the school
with a strap in his hand.
Who worries?
The one who is used to being hit
each and every day is the one who worries.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָשָׁל לְסוֹפֵר שֶׁבָּא לְבֵית הַסֵּפֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי מאיר's reason with a parable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one who is used to punishment is the one who fears a general warning sign.

steps.title: Sun eclipse warns the nations, moon eclipse warns ישראל
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא splits the signs: a sun eclipse is bad for the nations, and a moon eclipse is bad for ישראל, because ישראל count by the moon and the nations by the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: when the sun is eclipsed, it is a bad sign for the nations. When the moon is eclipsed, it is a bad sign for ישראל. This is because ישראל count their calendar by the moon, and the nations by the sun.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that gives a more detailed picture than רבי מאיר. It assigns each kind of eclipse to a different group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said any eclipse worries ישראל. This ברייתא says the sun belongs to the nations and the moon to ישראל, based on whose calendar each one runs. So each eclipse warns the people who 'count by' that light.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: when the sun is eclipsed
it is a bad sign for the nations.
When the moon is eclipsed
it is a bad sign for the enemies of Israel (meaning Israel itself).
Because Israel counts by the moon,
and the nations by the sun.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: מימרא (a parallel ברייתא with a different view than רבי מאיר)
steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַחַמָּה לוֹקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a more detailed system than רבי מאיר's general statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sun eclipse is a bad sign for the nations. A moon eclipse is a bad sign for ישראל.

steps.title: Where in the sky the eclipse happens
steps.stepSummary: An eclipse in the east warns people in the east, one in the west warns people in the west, and one in the middle of the sky warns the whole world.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is eclipsed in the east, it is a bad sign for those who live in the east. In the west, a bad sign for those who live in the west. In the middle of the sky, a bad sign for the entire world.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and adds that the place of the eclipse in the sky tells you which region is being warned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new detail: location narrows down who is affected. An eclipse in the middle of the sky is not limited to one direction, so it applies to everyone. This matches the earlier ברייתא that called a sun eclipse a bad sign for the whole world.

phrases.english: If it is eclipsed in the east
it is a bad sign for those who live in the east.
In the west: a bad sign for those who live in the west.
In the middle of the sky
a bad sign for the entire world.

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹקָה בַּמִּזְרָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the detail of location.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The location of the eclipse shows which region is being warned. The middle of the sky means the whole world.

steps.title: The color of the eclipse: war, hunger, or both
steps.stepSummary: If the eclipsed sun looks red like blood, war is coming. If it looks dark like sackcloth, hunger is coming. If it looks like both, both are coming.
steps.simpleTranslation: If its face looks like blood, war is coming to the world. Like sackcloth, arrows of hunger are coming to the world. Like this and like that, both war and arrows of hunger are coming to the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds that the color of the eclipse tells you what kind of trouble is coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Location told us who is warned. Color tells us what the trouble is. Red points to bloodshed (war), and dark sackcloth points to the darkened faces of hungry people (famine).

phrases.english: If its face looks like blood
the sword (war) is coming to the world.
Like sackcloth: arrows of hunger are coming to the world.
Like this one and like that one
both the sword and arrows of hunger are coming to the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּנָיו דּוֹמִין לְדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the detail of color.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Red means war, dark means famine, and both colors mean both troubles.

steps.title: The timing of the eclipse: slow or fast punishment
steps.stepSummary: An eclipse soon after sunrise means punishment will be slow to come. One near sunset means it will come quickly. Some say the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is eclipsed as it comes in (early in the day), punishment will delay in coming. As it goes out (late in the day), punishment will hurry to come. Some say it is the other way around.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds that the time of day of the eclipse tells you how soon the trouble will arrive. It also records a disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view says an early eclipse means the trouble is far off, and a late eclipse means it is near. The יש אומרים reverse it: early means fast, late means slow. This is a real disagreement, and the ברייתא does not decide it.

phrases.english: If it was eclipsed as it came in
punishment is delaying in coming.
As it goes out: it hurries to come.
And some say the matters are reversed.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָקָה בִּכְנִיסָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the detail of timing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Timing shows how soon the punishment comes. There are two opposite views on which time means what.

steps.title: When a nation is punished, its gods are punished too
steps.stepSummary: No nation is punished without its idols being punished along with it, as the פסוק says about the gods of מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no nation that is struck whose god is not struck along with it, as it says: 'And against all the gods of מצרים I will carry out judgments.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a related idea: when God punishes a nation, He also strikes the things that nation worships. It brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the sun eclipse: the nations count by the sun, and many worship it. When the sun is 'struck,' their god is struck along with them. The proof is יציאת מצרים, where God judged the gods of מצרים together with the people.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לְךָ כׇּל אוּמָּה וְאוּמָּהּ שֶׁלּוֹקָה,
phrases.english: And there is no nation at all that is struck
whose god is not struck together with it,
as it is said: 'And against all the gods of Egypt'
I will carry out judgments.'

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: ראיה (the statement is backed by a פסוק)
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לְךָ כׇּל אוּמָּה וְאוּמָּהּ שֶׁלּוֹקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a theological idea that explains why a sun eclipse is linked to the nations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a nation is punished, its object of worship is punished with it.

steps.title: ישראל who do God's will need not fear the signs
steps.stepSummary: When ישראל do God's will, they need not fear any of these signs. ירמיהו says only the nations are frightened by the signs of the heavens.
steps.simpleTranslation: When ישראל do the will of God, they do not fear any of these signs, as it says: 'So says ה׳: Do not learn the way of the nations, and do not be frightened by the signs of the heavens, for the nations are frightened by them.' The nations will be frightened, but ישראל will not be frightened.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends the whole eclipse discussion with a comforting conclusion. All these signs only have power over ישראל when they are not doing God's will.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the omens above (location, color, timing) are real warnings, but ישראל's fate depends on their behavior, not on the sky. The פסוק in ירמיהו tells ישראל not to copy the nations and not to be afraid of heavenly signs. The גמרא reads it closely: 'the nations will be frightened,' and ישראל will not.

keyTerms.meaning: The will of God (מָקוֹם is a name for God)

steps.whatToRemember: Eclipses are warning signs: the sun for the nations, the moon for ישראל, with details of place, color, and timing. But when ישראל do God's will, they have nothing to fear from any heavenly sign.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the Torah view on omens: ישראל's future is decided by their actions, not by the stars or the sky.

phrases.aramaic: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם
phrases.english: And when Israel does the will of God
they do not fear any of these,
as it is said: 'So says ה׳:'
Do not learn the way of the nations,
and do not be frightened by the signs of the heavens,
for the nations are frightened by them.'
The nations will be frightened, but Israel will not be frightened.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the eclipse discussion by limiting the power of the omens.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Heavenly signs have no power to frighten ישראל when they do God's will. Only the nations need fear them.

steps.title: Four sins that cause the sun to be eclipsed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists four sins that cause a solar eclipse: an אב בית דין who is not eulogized properly, a נערה המאורסה who cried out with no one to save her, משכב זכור, and two brothers killed together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Because of four things the sun is eclipsed. When the head of the court dies and is not properly mourned. When a betrothed girl screams in the city and no one comes to save her. Because of male relations. And when two brothers are killed together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes a ברייתא that explains what causes a solar eclipse. It gives a list of four sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps explained what an eclipse warns about. This step adds new information about why eclipses happen: specific sins in society bring them. The first cause is a kind of insult to a great Torah leader, so the heavens eulogize him when people fail to do it properly.

keyTerms.meaning: The sun is eclipsed (literally, "the sun is struck")
Head of the court, second in rank to the נשיא

steps.confusionAlert: תנו רבנן introduces a ברייתא from the time of the משנה, not a statement by a later אמורא. That gives it extra weight.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Because of four things the sun is eclipsed:
over a head of the court who died
phrases.notes: The eclipse acts as a heavenly eulogy for him

phrases.english: and is not eulogized properly,
and over a betrothed girl who screamed in the city
phrases.notes: She screamed because she was being attacked

phrases.english: and there was no one to save her,
and over male relations,
and over two brothers
whose blood was spilled together.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בִּשְׁבִיל אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים חַמָּה לוֹקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from what eclipses signal (Steps 16-25) to what sins cause them
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four specific sins cause the sun to be eclipsed

steps.title: Four sins that cause the heavenly lights to be eclipsed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with four sins that cause the מאורות to be eclipsed: forging defaming letters, giving עדות שקר, raising small animals in ארץ ישראל, and cutting down good fruit trees.
steps.simpleTranslation: And because of four things the heavenly lights are eclipsed. Because of people who write forged letters to defame others. Because of people who give false testimony. Because of people who raise sheep and goats in ארץ ישראל. And because of people who cut down good fruit trees.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second list of four sins. This time they cause the מאורות to be eclipsed, which רש״י explains as the moon and the stars, as opposed to the sun in step 26.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of these sins harm other people or the land. Forgery and false testimony hurt people through lies. Small animals graze in other people's fields and damage them, and cutting down fruit trees destroys something useful.

keyTerms.meaning: The heavenly lights (רש״י: the moon and the stars)
A forged document, such as a letter written to defame someone
Small domestic animals, like sheep and goats

steps.confusionAlert: This is a separate list from Step 26. Step 26 is about the sun alone (חמה). This list is about the מאורות, which רש״י explains as the moon and the stars (מאורות – ירח וכוכבים).

phrases.english: And because of four things the heavenly lights are eclipsed:
over writers of forged documents,
phrases.notes: Fake letters meant to ruin someone's name

phrases.english: and over those who give false testimony,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל מְגַדְּלֵי בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: and over those who raise small animals in the Land of Israel,
phrases.notes: In settled areas, where they graze in other people's fields

phrases.english: and over those who cut down good trees.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִשְׁבִיל אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים מְאוֹרוֹת לוֹקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second list in the same ברייתא, parallel in form to Step 26
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four sins of harming others cause the heavenly lights to be eclipsed

steps.title: Sins that cause homeowners' property to be taken by the government
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins a third list of four sins that cause homeowners' property to be handed to the מלכות. It starts with keeping paid-up loan documents and lending with רבית, and the list continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And because of four things, the property of homeowners is handed over to the government: because of people who keep loan documents that were already paid off, and because of people who lend with interest...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts a third list of four sins. This time the punishment is not an eclipse but losing property to the government. Only two items appear here, and the list continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These sins are about money gained unfairly. A lender who keeps a שטר after it was paid could use it to collect a second time. A lender who charges רבית takes money he is not entitled to, so he loses his own money as a fitting punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: Loan documents that have already been paid off
Interest on a loan, forbidden by the Torah between Jews

steps.confusionAlert: This list is not finished. The ברייתא promised four items, and only two appear here. The other two come on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: And because of four things
the property of homeowners is handed over to the government:
over those who keep paid-off loan documents,
phrases.notes: Instead of tearing them up or returning them, which lets them collect twice

phrases.english: and over those who lend with interest,

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִשְׁבִיל אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים נִכְסֵי בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים נִמְסָרִין לַמַּלְכוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third list in the same ברייתא. It shifts from heavenly signs to a financial punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sins of unfair money-taking, such as keeping paid notes and lending with רבית, cause homeowners to lose property to the government
